about.title: About the Conference
about.desc1: Preserving Heritage, Powering Innovation: Tamil–Welsh Conference on Digital Futures for Minority Languages is an international platform that brings together researchers, educators, technologists, policymakers, industry leaders, and students to explore how digital technologies can safeguard and strengthen minority languages in the AI era.
about.desc2: The conference celebrates the shared journeys of Tamil, one of the world's oldest living classical languages, and Welsh (Cymraeg), a revitalized minority language with globally recognized bilingual education and language policy initiatives. Though separated by geography and linguistic ancestry, both languages demonstrate how community action, education, and technology can ensure linguistic resilience for future generations.
about.visionDesc: To create a lasting Tamil–Welsh partnership that transforms minority-language research into practical digital solutions for education, governance, culture, and industry.
about.whyDesc: Tamil and Welsh have followed different historical paths but share a common mission: ensuring that language thrives in the digital age. Welsh has expanded bilingual education, community engagement, and digital language standards across universities and public institutions, while Tamil has built a rich ecosystem of computing standards, language resources, and international collaboration through initiatives such as INFITT.
objectives: Advance AI and Language Technology for minority languages.
Promote collaborative research between Tamil Nadu and Wales.
Showcase innovations in NLP, Speech Technology, and Digital Humanities.
Support open datasets, digital archives, and language resources.
Build international academic and industry partnerships.
Inspire students and young researchers to contribute to language technology.
